# ARC

1. Every autumn Grossvater Hans sits alone on the high, dry Herbstfelsen with empty hands and hums the first half of a song that the mermaid Mira sang to him as a boy until the tide carried her off, so he has waited for a word from her ever since, while down at the shore Emma, who knows his half by heart, hums it too beside Noah, Mama Sarah and Papa Daniel, holds the shiny chestnut she found on the path so tight that Noah never gets a turn, and takes Noah's hand whenever it gets dark.
2. When the old sea turtle Kora, who comes to the lowest stone every autumn and always leaves at last light, rises there with the first notes of Mira's answer, which begin exactly where Grossvater's half always stops, only Emma hears them, because Grossvater's old ears cannot catch them over the surf and his stiff knees cannot climb down to the water.
3. So Emma runs onto the wet stones although Mama Sarah, Papa Daniel and Noah call her back because the stones are slippery and the water is cold and deep, and when Kora looks at her once and dives away, Emma hops on to the last stone, hums Grossvater's half, and stretches both arms over the gap where the next stone is missing.
4. Kora, who dived only to see whether the child would follow, rises under her hands, Emma clings to the shell, and Noah, who has just called her back, jumps after her and grabs the rim because he will not let her go alone, so Kora dives with both of them while Mama Sarah and Papa Daniel stay at the last stone, because no grown-up can follow into cold deep water on a shell that is wide enough for two small children.
5. Because one hand on Kora's shell lets them breathe and hear under the sea, the children ride down through a coral archway into Mira's reef below the Herbstfelsen, where Mira, who can never go up, sings Grossvater's missing half into a shell because Kora has only flippers and cannot carry it to the stone, hangs it on a cord round Emma's neck because Emma is the one who hummed, and says it answers only when it hears the first half of the song.
6. Mira tells them to go now because the water has gone dark earlier than expected and Kora must leave with the evening current at last light, but before they start up, a small octopus who lives in the reef says his name is Oskar and that nobody has time to play, and pokes at Emma's chestnut, and Emma pulls it away.
7. On the way up Oskar slips the cord from Emma's neck, squirts ink and calls "Find it!", and the water turns black.
8. Noah, who cannot stand to lose, grabs at the ink again and again and catches only water, Kora says the current will turn soon and then she cannot bring them back to the lowest stone, and Emma, who has lost Noah's hand, is alone in the dark she fears and thinks Grossvater will wait another year.
9. But Emma remembers what Mira said, that the shell answers only when it hears the first half of the song, so she hums it out loud, alone in the dark, and a faint hum answers from a crack in the reef.
10. Emma points and tells Kora where the hum comes from, Kora turns toward it, and Noah reaches into the crack and pulls the cord, but Oskar holds the other end with all eight arms and will not let go.
11. Because Oskar wants only something round to hide and find, Emma holds out the chestnut that she would never share with Noah, Oskar takes it and lets go, and Noah pulls the shell out and hangs it on Emma's neck again.
12. Kora swims up through the last of the light with Oskar, who wants to see where his chestnut came from, riding on her shell, and Mama Sarah sees the shell rise and calls, Papa Daniel lifts both children over the gap to the last stone, Mama Sarah holds them and says never again onto the wet stones without a grown-up.
13. Emma walks up the wet stones with her hand in Papa's and puts the shell into Grossvater's hands, Grossvater hums the first half, and the shell answers with Mira's second half, so that his hands are empty no more and Emma feels proud and happy.
14. Kora, who stays one more breath because after fifty autumns she wants to hear the song end, hears the finished song ring down from the Herbstfelsen, and Mira's face rises in the water beside her, Emma calls "Danke, Mira!" and Mira lifts a hand, then Emma calls "Bis zum nächsten Herbst, Kora!" and Kora lifts a flipper and swims into the dusk while Oskar waves the chestnut from her shell and Emma smiles, because he may keep it.
